name: Pneumo-AI
tagline: Deep learning application for classifying chest X-rays using VGG19 transfer learning
about: Pneumo-AI is an end-to-end deep learning project exploring automated chest X-ray classification into NORMAL and PNEUMONIA categories. The system integrates a VGG19 transfer-learning pipeline with an interactive Streamlit analytics dashboard for model predictions and visual evaluation.

architecture.summary: An automated medical image classification workflow integrating an image preprocessing pipeline, a VGG19 transfer learning feature extractor with custom classification head, and a Streamlit dashboard with Plotly visual analytics.

flows.title: Path B: Visual Analytics & Model Evaluation

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Pneumo-AI is an applied deep learning project designed to evaluate automated image classification of pediatric and adult chest radiographs. By pairing a convolutional neural network architecture with transfer learning techniques, the project explores how computational vision can assist with preliminary radiographic categorization into NORMAL or PNEUMONIA classifications.

The project incorporates an end-to-end user application developed with Streamlit, enabling users to upload radiographs, trigger inference, inspect model confidence scores, and review detailed analytical metrics.

sections.heading: The Problem
sections.body:
Pneumonia remains a leading cause of hospital admissions and mortality worldwide. Accurate diagnosis depends heavily on radiological interpretation of chest X-rays, identifying consolidation, ground-glass opacities, or pleural effusions.

In resource-constrained clinical settings or rural healthcare centers where certified radiologists may not be available around the clock, manual interpretation workflows create diagnostic bottlenecks. Developing reliable computer-assisted screening workflows provides an avenue to accelerate triage and support clinical decision-making.

sections.heading: The Solution & Transfer Learning Strategy
sections.body:
Training a deep convolutional neural network entirely from scratch on medical imagery frequently leads to overfitting due to limited dataset sizes and high anatomical variance. Pneumo-AI mitigates this through transfer learning using VGG19 pretrained on the extensive ImageNet dataset.

The feature extraction layers are frozen to leverage general low-level geometric and textural filters (edges, textures, contours), while custom fully-connected dense layers are appended and fine-tuned specifically to distinguish radiographic opacities characteristic of pneumonia.

sections.heading: System Architecture & Data Flows
sections.body: The application separates image acquisition and transformation from neural inference, while maintaining a parallel evaluation pipeline for inspecting confusion matrices and loss curves.

sections.heading: Technical Pipeline & Image Processing
sections.body:
Chest Radiograph (DICOM / PNG / JPEG)
        ↓
Streamlit Drag-and-Drop Upload
        ↓
Dimensions Resized to 128 × 128
        ↓
3-Channel Grayscale-to-RGB Conversion
        ↓
Pixel Normalization (Scaling to [0, 1])
        ↓
VGG19 Feature Extraction Backbone
        ↓
Classification Head (Dense + Softmax)
        ↓
NORMAL vs PNEUMONIA Prediction
        ↓
Confidence Score & Plotly Visual Analytics

sections.heading: Neural Network Architecture
sections.body:
Input Layer (128 × 128 × 3 RGB Tensor)
        ↓
VGG19 Convolutional Blocks (Pretrained ImageNet)
  - 16 Convolutional Layers (3×3 Filters)
  - Max Pooling Layers (2×2 Stride)
        ↓
Flatten Layer (Vector Dimension: 4608)
        ↓
Dense Layer (4608 Units + ReLU Activation)
        ↓
Dense Output Layer (2 Units + Softmax Activation)
        ↓
Class Probabilities: [P(Normal), P(Pneumonia)]
sections.note: Architecture parameters are documented in the project's repository and implemented with TensorFlow Keras.

sections.heading: Interactive Streamlit Analytics Dashboard
sections.body:
To make model outputs transparent and interpretable, the application is presented via an interactive Streamlit dashboard structured into three distinct views:

1. Prediction View: Allows users to drag-and-drop chest X-ray images, triggering automated preprocessing and displaying real-time predictions with categorical confidence meters.
2. Data Analytics View: Explores the training dataset distribution, class balances, and sample inspection across both target classes.
3. Performance View: Integrates Plotly charts visualizing validation accuracy, loss progression over epochs, confusion matrices, and precision/recall trade-offs.

sections.heading: Key Features & Workflow Capabilities
sections.body:
Drag-and-drop chest X-ray image upload interface
Automated image standardization (resizing, channel expansion, normalization)
Real-time deep learning inference using TensorFlow / Keras
Confidence score indicators and class probability distributions
Interactive confusion matrix displaying false positive and false negative rates
Training and validation curve visualizations
Model-performance metrics dashboard powered by Plotly
Cached model weights utilizing Streamlit cache mechanisms for instant execution

sections.heading: Results & Evaluation Metrics
sections.note: The project reports approximately 91% test accuracy on its test split. The repository dashboard exposes detailed metrics including precision, recall, F1 score, specificity, and confusion matrix analytics.

sections.heading: Technical Challenges & Input Normalization
sections.body:
Medical imaging datasets present significant challenges with data heterogeneity: varying resolutions, varying exposures, differences in patient positioning, and artifacts from medical equipment.

A primary challenge was engineering a deterministic preprocessing pipeline in Python that reliably standardizes disparate input images into uniform 128×128 tensors with proper numerical scaling without distorting critical diagnostic lung parenchyma.

sections.heading: Educational Scope & Medical Disclaimer
sections.body:
This project is developed exclusively for academic, engineering, and educational purposes to demonstrate deep learning transfer learning techniques on computer vision datasets.

It is not a clinically validated diagnostic tool and must not be used as a substitute for professional medical evaluation, diagnosis, or radiological assessment by licensed practitioners.

sections.heading: Outcome & Research Learnings
sections.body: Pneumo-AI demonstrates how convolutional transfer learning pipelines can be combined with user-friendly web interfaces to produce interactive machine learning tooling. The project highlighted the practical engineering challenges of preparing medical datasets, managing inference latency, and designing clear interfaces for probabilistic models.
